‘which contain the terrible and important news of Manchester. These are, as it were, the
distant thunders of the terrible storm which is approaching. The tyrants here, as in the
French Revolution, have first shed blood. May their execrable lessons not be learnt with
equal docility!’ (L ii 119). In this mood of mixed outrage and foreboding S. quickly began
to draft MA, possibly as early as 5 September, but perhaps a week or even more later. He
clearly wished to appeal without delay to a broad popular audience of those who stood
to gain directly from fundamental reform at what appeared to be a decisive juncture in
English political life, and on 23 September the 372 lines of the finished poem were posted to
Leigh Hunt (Mary Jnl i 298) for publication in the Examiner. (As Mary remarks in a letter
